repo_model.summary: This repository is now a trial2vec-based RelBench study-outcome solution rather than a trivial baseline. main.py configures the runtime and delegates to trial2vec_pipeline.py, which builds temporally censored BiomedBERT field banks, retrieval and structured features, training-only OOF heads, separate validation/test prediction chains, and an optional gated chronological neural stage before writing the official prediction artifacts.

book.summary: This repository is now a trial2vec-based RelBench study-outcome solution rather than a trivial baseline. main.py configures the runtime and delegates to trial2vec_pipeline.py, which builds temporally censored BiomedBERT field banks, retrieval and structured features, training-only OOF heads, separate validation/test prediction chains, and an optional gated chronological neural stage before writing the official prediction artifacts.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: A thin launcher runs a cached, temporally censored text-and-structured-feature pipeline whose predictions are scored by the immutable evaluator.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the thin main.py launcher directly for debug or full inference, then use the provided evaluator for official scoring.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Make modeling and feature changes in trial2vec_pipeline.py while keeping main.py as a minimal launcher and preserving the existing prediction contract.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction alignment, temporal censoring, train-only model selection, and validation-only scoring are hard contracts.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Gate the expensive pipeline with debug, throughput, forward-fold, and final contract checks before trusting validation metrics.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: Debug limits, optional Stage-B rejection, cache layout, temporal row order, and validation uncertainty can all affect interpretation.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The pipeline combines DuckDB/parquet data access, scientific Python and scikit-learn heads, PyTorch training, and Hugging Face BiomedBERT.

experiments.solution_spec:
# Temporally streamed Trial2Vec-style field encoder

## Core Idea

Learn trial-level representations from the sanitized 250,000-study corpus using field-aware contrastive self-supervision, then retrieve completed historical trials as evidence and fine-tune a ranking classifier. Build a frozen-field fallback first, because full self-supervised adaptation is the highest-ceiling but highest-risk lane.

Expected ceiling: approximately 0.78–0.83 if corpus-level adaptation works; lower probability than the first three lanes because of implementation and runtime risk.

## Implementation

1. Construct chronological trial records:

   - Registration fields: title, summaries, eligibility sections, design, conditions, interventions, sponsor, and site summaries.
   - Historical evidence fields: primary-outcome text, valid analyses, dropout, and adverse events only after their recorded date.
   - Create separate model-A data ending at 2020-01-01 and model-B data ending at 2021-01-01.

2. Initialize field encoders from BiomedBERT. Do not call Trial2Vec’s `from_pretrained`, download its NCT embedding table, or import any outcome checkpoint. Use the public Trial2Vec work only as an architectural reference; its paper establishes field-aware contrastive learning and downstream outcome use. [Trial2Vec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.14719), [package documentation](https://pypi.org/project/Trial2Vec/)

3. Stage A, which must bank first:

   - Freeze BiomedBERT.
   - Encode at most five 256-token field chunks per trial.
   - Project field vectors to 256 dimensions.
   - Train a two-layer attention/set pooler with same-trial field contrast, masked-field reconstruction, and condition/intervention-linked positives.
   - Produce retrieval and structured features, then train a ridge classifier.

4. Stage B:

   - Add LoRA to the last two encoder layers.
   - Continue contrastive training chronologically with same-phase/year hard negatives.
   - Save checkpoints at internal forward-fold cutoffs so no checkpoint sees future-dated rows relative to its evaluation fold.
   - Keep Stage B only if it beats Stage A by more than training-fold uncertainty.

5. For each seed, retrieve 32 completed historical trials available by that timestamp. Evidence tokens contain similarity, age, known success, analysis count, minimum p-value, dropout, and serious-event burden. Exclude the query trial.

6. Fuse current field tokens and historical evidence with a small gated attention module. Concatenate a structured residual branch containing phase, enrollment, arms, masking, ages, site diversity, and hierarchical historical priors.

7. Fine-tune the pooler, gate, LoRA parameters, and classifier using BCE plus a modest pairwise ranking loss among positive/negative rows at the same timestamp. Use modality dropout to reduce dependence on sponsor or disease identity.

8. Blend the neural model with the Stage-A ridge baseline using training OOF predictions only.

9. Produce model A from data and labels legally available for the validation chain, save validation predictions, then produce model B using train plus validation labels and records available at the test cutoff. Never overwrite model A’s validation predictions.

10. At 3.0 hours, stop optional adaptation and use the best completed Stage-A or Stage-B checkpoint, preserving an hour for inference and contract checks.

## Hyperparameters

- Backbone: BiomedBERT base
- Field chunks: maximum 5 × 256 tokens
- Trial embedding: 256 dimensions
- Pooler: 2 layers, 4 heads
- Retrieval neighbors: 32
- LoRA: rank 8, alpha 16, dropout 0.1
- Contrastive temperature: 0.07
- Self-supervised batch: 128 trials
- Supervised batch: 32
- LoRA learning rate: `2e-4`
- Head/pooler learning rate: `6e-4`
- Supervised epochs: 5
- Pairwise-ranking weight: 0.15
- Modality dropout: 0.2
- Weight decay: 0.02
- Gradient clipping: 1.0

## Runtime and staging

- Frozen field encoding and Stage-A bank: 60–90 minutes.
- Contrastive pooler and retrieval: 30–45 minutes.
- Optional LoRA and supervised fusion: 60–90 minutes.
- Hard stop: three hours for training; final hour reserved for A/B inference and output verification.
- Debug: 2,000 unlabeled studies, frozen encoder, four neighbors, one pooler epoch, and a ridge head.

# Coverage

- **Input distribution — MEASURED:** The database contains roughly 250,000 unlabeled studies and about 12,000 labeled training seeds, supporting corpus pretraining followed by modest supervised adaptation.
- **Schema coverage — MEASURED:** Registration tokens cover every start-time table; structured residuals and historical evidence incorporate all completion-time tables.
- **Temporal safety — MEASURED:** Model-A and model-B corpora have separate temporal cutoffs. Historical evidence requires `date <= t`, and no NCT-specific pretrained artifact is used.
- **Self-supervised transfer — ASSUMED:** Field contrast and masked-field learning on this sanitized corpus will improve outcome ranking over frozen embeddings.
- **Runtime — ASSUMED:** Five short chunks per trial and LoRA-only adaptation fit the A100 budget. Stage A and the three-hour cutoff protect against failure.
- **Metric mechanics — MEASURED:** Architecture retention, checkpoint choice, and blending use training-only forward folds; pairwise loss targets within-cohort ordering.
- **Harness/output — MEASURED:** Model A writes untouched validation predictions; model B writes test predictions after train-plus-validation refitting.
- **Permitted data — MEASURED:** Only sanitized AACT records and general biomedical pretrained weights are used; external Trial2Vec embeddings and outcome weights are explicitly prohibited.
